newsitem.title: UK: UK's Oftel demands review of BT IDN prices.
newsitem.headline: UK's Oftel demands review of BT IDN prices.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc is reviewing the prices it charges for integrated digital network services following complaints from industry watchdog Oftel that its tariffs were discriminatory.

Oftel said its director general Don Cruickshank has asked BT to review its tariffs, which he said were likely to have anti-competitive effects on customers and BT's competitors who provide a similar service.
"I am determined that customers should face no material obstacles in choosing service providers other than BT," he said in a statement.
BT's integrated services digital network is used by many small businesses, schools and some individuals to access the so-called information superhighway.
Cruickshank said he had given BT a few days to meet his demands. "I expect BT to meet its commitments through price reductions," he said in a statement.
Concerns about BT's position as the dominant supplier in this area and its prices were raised during the recent price control review by consumers and by the government.
